title: AIBE Strategy, Tips & Tricks
description: Action-oriented preparation guidance derived from the supplied previous-paper analysis material and the question bank. This is a study aid, not an official BCI instruction.
sourceBasis: Supplied Paperathon material: previous papers are better analysed subject-wise rather than only year-wise; link related provisions/concepts while solving MCQs.
Supplied Paperathon material: use subject-wise weightage analysis to prioritize preparation.
Current AIBE XXI paper analysis: the paper is organized across major civil, criminal, minor, technical and other law areas, with explicit question distribution.
Current AIBE XXII syllabus supplied by the user: 19 subject groups and 100 total questions.

strategies.title: Study by subject, not only by year
strategies.why: Year-wise papers show what was asked. Subject-wise analysis shows where repeated testing and weightage concentrate.
action: Build subject-wise practice sets from the common question bank.
After every mock, move wrong answers into the relevant subject/topic queue.
Use full previous papers only after targeted subject practice.

strategies.title: Link provisions while solving
strategies.why: The supplied Paperathon approach recommends connecting the tested provision with related provisions and concepts.
action: When a question tests one section, note two or three closely related provisions.
Group similar doctrines, exceptions and procedural rules.
Turn each wrong answer into a small linked-law note.

strategies.title: Use weightage to allocate time
strategies.why: The supplied analysis material contains exam-wise subject weightage tables.
action: Prioritize high-frequency subjects first.
Give smaller subjects shorter but repeated revision cycles.
Do not ignore low-weight subjects because they can still provide easy marks.

strategies.title: Separate learning from testing
strategies.why: Solving papers alone can hide knowledge gaps.
action: Learn a topic first.
Do 20-30 topic MCQs.
Review every wrong and guessed answer.
Then attempt a timed mixed set.

strategies.title: Recent-law revision
strategies.why: Recent papers contain newer statutory frameworks such as BNS, BNSS and BSA.
action: Give special revision time to newly applicable legislation.
Compare old and new provisions where the question bank contains both.
Practice questions that test transition, definitions, sections and procedural changes.

strategies.title: Use the 3-hour mock deliberately
strategies.why: The supplied AIBE XXI paper states 100 questions, 1 mark each, no negative marking and 3 hours.
action: Run full 100-question mocks under the same time limit.
Use a first-pass strategy for confident questions.
Flag uncertain questions and return later.
Reserve a final review window for unanswered questions.

strategies.title: Exploit no-negative-marking
strategies.why: For the supplied AIBE XXI paper, there is no negative marking.
action: Never leave a question unanswered in the final submission.
First eliminate clearly wrong options.
If uncertain, make the best-supported choice before time expires.

strategies.title: Build a mistake-driven revision loop
strategies.why: The most useful personal signal is what the student repeatedly gets wrong.
action: Store wrong, skipped and guessed questions locally.
Create a Practice My Mistakes mode.
Repeat until the same concept is consistently answered correctly.

strategies.title: Use question-type patterns
strategies.why: The supplied papers include direct MCQs, assertion-reason, statement/conclusion and scenario-based questions.
action: Practice each question type separately.
For assertion-reason questions, judge A and R independently before checking the relationship.
For statement questions, evaluate each statement before selecting the combined option.

strategies.title: Final-week execution
strategies.why: At the end, additional broad reading often gives less return than targeted correction.
action: Stop expanding the syllabus.
Run mixed timed sets.
Revise mistakes, high-frequency provisions and recent-law changes.
Complete at least one full mock under exam conditions.

appScreens.name: Subject Priority
appScreens.behavior: Show priority based on configured syllabus/question distribution, but label historical frequency as historical evidence rather than a prediction.

appScreens.name: Practice My Mistakes
appScreens.behavior: Link directly to questions the student got wrong, skipped or repeatedly guessed.

guardrails: Do not claim that past frequency guarantees future questions.
Do not present third-party preparation advice as official BCI rules.
Do not reproduce the supplied publisher text verbatim.
Keep source-derived observations separate from app-generated recommendations.
